stem: By what age does a typical child cease to have any daytime sleep (naps)?
explanation: The lecturer states that usually a 4-year-old will not have any daytime sleep, marking a transition from early childhood patterns.
rationale: This transition usually occurs just before or around the time children start preschool.

optionExplanations.A: At 2 years of age, infants still spend roughly 10 hours asleep, but the transition to zero daytime sleep occurs later.
optionExplanations.B: Daytime sleep begins to reduce significantly by age 3, but the full cessation usually happens in the following year.
optionExplanations.C: The lecturer states that usually a 4-year-old will not have any daytime sleep, marking a transition from early childhood patterns.
optionExplanations.D: While schooling might enforce this, the physiological transition to no naps typically occurs earlier than age 6.

source.hint: This transition usually occurs just before or around the time children start preschool.
